request.prompt: Which humanoid robots have SDK access?

result.text:
Several humanoid and bipedal robot platforms provide software development kits (SDKs), application programming interfaces (APIs), or open-source frameworks for developers, researchers, and engineers.

Key humanoid robots with developer access include:

1. Unitree Robotics (H1 & G1 Series)

SDK Details: Unitree provides robust developer tools, notably unitree_sdk2 and ROS/ROS2 integration packages (unitree_ros2). They also offer simulation support through MuJoCo (unitree_mujoco).

Access Level: Allows developers to work with high-level control (point-to-point motion) as well as low-level joint/motor communication protocols, making it popular for academic research and machine learning (imitation learning frameworks like LeRobot).

2. PAL Robotics (TALOS & REEM-C)

SDK Details: PAL Robotics designs its research humanoids to run natively on ROS (Robot Operating System) and ROS 2.

Access Level They Provide: Full source code and simulation models (Gazebo), giving researchers deep control over kinematics, motion planning (MoveIt), computer vision, and balance algorithms.

3. UBTECH Robotics (Walker Series)

SDK Details: UBTECH provides SDKs targeted at institutional research partners and enterprise developers working with their Walker line of full-size humanoids.

Access Level: Focuses on human-robot interaction, navigation, and task execution APIs.

4. Open-Source Ecosystems & Reference Platforms (NVIDIA Isaac GR00T)

Rather than a single robot, companies building humanoids often plug into standardized developer stacks:

NVIDIA Isaac Sim / GR00T: A comprehensive platform and reference workflow used by various emerging humanoid developers (such as Agile Robots' Agile ONE) to train general-purpose foundation models, test behaviors in simulation, and deploy via the Jetson Thor edge computing architecture.

ROS / ROS 2: The de facto standard middleware framework used across almost all open-access humanoid hardware for controlling actuators, processing camera/depth feeds, and executing Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM).

Note: Many advanced commercial humanoid companies (such as Figure AI or Boston Dynamics with Atlas) tightly control their software stacks in-house or restrict SDK access to select enterprise partners.

Are you looking for an SDK to use for academic research, simulation, or a specific commercial hardware platform?

### 1\. Unitree Robotics (H1 & G1 Series)

They also offer simulation support through MuJoCo (`unitree_mujoco`).
